evals.prompt: Make this existing dashboard work well from narrow mobile browser widths through large desktop screens without changing its product behavior.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering activates, inspects existing design, and reasons about responsive/adaptive layout and input behavior.

evals.prompt: Use ui-engineering to refine this desktop settings page while preserving our existing DESIGN.md.
evals.expected_output: The project design system remains authoritative and refinement stays proportional.

evals.prompt: A queue consumer duplicates jobs after retry; find the root cause.
Design a WebView checkout screen where native owns authentication and deep links but web owns navigation inside checkout.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering makes the native/web ownership boundary explicit and reports supporting integration/security concerns where relevant.

evals.prompt: Impeccable is installed, but DESIGN.md requires subtle dense desktop UI. Improve typography and spacing.
evals.expected_output: The provider may be composed for typography/layout but DESIGN.md remains authoritative and no new visual direction is invented.

evals.prompt: Review a track actions menu that works with mouse but cannot be opened from keyboard.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering treats keyboard accessibility as product behavior and verifies the relevant interaction.

evals.prompt: Use ui-engineering for a new responsive web product with no component library or CSS strategy selected yet. It needs custom visual identity, dark mode, dialogs, menus, forms, keyboard accessibility, and touch support.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering compares custom, headless-primitives, styled-library, and hybrid strategies against the product's design/accessibility needs instead of defaulting to a popular library. It distinguishes any pervasive architecture-level choice from reversible package details.

evals.prompt: Build the UI foundation for a new app. Tailwind and a shadcn-style library are popular but the project has not selected them.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering does not adopt Tailwind or a component library by popularity/default. It derives component and styling strategy from product/design requirements and existing DESIGN.md truth.

evals.prompt: The product needs custom visual styling but several complex dialogs, menus, popovers, and comboboxes with strong keyboard and screen-reader behavior.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering seriously considers maintained headless/accessibility primitives to reduce interaction risk while keeping the visual language project-owned; it does not insist on hand-rolling all primitives or importing a full styled system.
